subject: physics_2
question_text: What is a zener diode? Explain how it is used as a voltage Regulator.

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two figures carry 0 marks because the question does not ask for a diagram. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked against the book (p.56): Kirchhoff's current law at the junction gives the supply current as the sum of the zener current and the load current; Kirchhoff's voltage law round the input loop gives the input voltage as the drop across the series resistance plus the zener voltage, which is also the output voltage. With the input voltage held fixed the supply current is fixed, so a change in load current is met by an equal and opposite change in zener current. With the load fixed, a change in supply current is taken entirely by the zener. The book writes the series resistance as R in the voltage-law line and as the series resistance elsewhere; the same symbol is used throughout here. Symbols with capital-letter subscripts are authored as KaTeX, which Unicode cannot encode honestly. Both figures were rendered and inspected before this card was filed.

recall_prompt: Define a zener diode, then explain regulation for a changing load and for a changing input voltage.

steps.label: Zener diode
lines: A zener diode is a heavily doped p-n
junction diode which has a sharp
breakdown voltage when it is operated in
reverse bias.
A voltage regulator is a device that gives
a constant output voltage even when the
input voltage or the load current changes.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Heavily doped, sharp breakdown, reverse bias — and the regulator definition.
steps.why: Heavy doping is what makes the breakdown sharp and repeatable at a fixed voltage. That fixed voltage is the whole basis of the regulator, so the definition and the application are one idea, not two.
common_mistakes: Leaving out reverse bias. In forward bias a zener diode is an ordinary diode.
Saying it is lightly doped. Light doping gives avalanche breakdown, not zener breakdown.

recall.must_convey: That a zener diode is a heavily doped p-n junction diode with a sharp breakdown voltage in reverse bias.
accept: heavily doped p n junction diode
properly doped diode with a fixed breakdown voltage
reject: supply current equals zener current plus load current

steps.memory_tip: Heavily doped → thin layer → sharp breakdown → fixed voltage.

steps.label: Zener symbol
steps.margin_note: An ordinary diode symbol with the bar bent at both ends. The bent bar is what marks it as a zener.
steps.why: The bent ends are the only difference from the ordinary diode symbol, so drawing a plain straight bar draws the wrong device.
common_mistakes: Drawing a plain straight bar. That is an ordinary diode.
Bending both ends the same way. The two bends go opposite ways.

recall.must_convey: That the zener symbol is the diode symbol with the bar bent at both ends.
accept: diode symbol with a bent bar
triangle with a z shaped bar
arrow and bar with turned ends
reject: series resistance and a load resistance

steps.memory_tip: The bar is bent into a Z — Z for zener.

steps.label: Regulator circuit
steps.margin_note: The zener sits across the load, in reverse bias. The series resistance limits the current and takes the extra voltage.
steps.why: Two features of the circuit do all the work: the zener is in parallel with the load, so it fixes the load voltage; and the series resistance is in the supply line, so any extra input voltage is dropped across it and never reaches the load.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the series resistance. Without it the breakdown current is not limited and the diode is damaged.
Connecting the zener in forward bias. The bar must face the positive side of the supply.
Putting the zener in series with the load instead of across it.

recall.must_convey: That the circuit has a series resistance from the supply, with the zener in reverse across the load.
accept: series resistance then zener across the load
zener in parallel with the load resistance
draw the supply, the series resistor and the zener
reject: the input voltage equals the drop plus the zener voltage

steps.memory_tip: Series resistor takes the extra volts; the zener holds the rest steady.

steps.label: Circuit equations
lines: By Kirchhoff's current law at the junction:
By Kirchhoff's voltage law in the input
loop:

lines.text: V_{in} = I R_s + V_Z, \quad V_Z = V_o \qquad \dots (2)

lines: The output is taken across the zener, so
the output voltage is the zener voltage.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both laws written, and the statement that the output voltage IS the zener voltage.
steps.why: Equation (2) is the whole reason the circuit regulates: the output is taken directly across the zener, so as long as the diode stays in breakdown the output voltage cannot be anything except the zener voltage.
common_mistakes: Writing the supply current as the load current alone. Part of it passes through the zener.
Forgetting the drop across the series resistance in the voltage law.

recall.must_convey: That the supply current is the sum of the zener and load currents, and the input voltage is the drop across the series resistance plus the zener voltage, which is the output.
accept: I equals I zener plus I load
input voltage equals I R plus zener voltage
reject: as the load resistance rises the load current falls

steps.memory_tip: One current splits two ways; one voltage divides between the resistor and the diode.

steps.label: Load changes
lines: From (1), with the supply current fixed:
If the load resistance increases, the load
current decreases. The zener current then
increases by the same amount, so the
total current and the output voltage
stay constant.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The minus sign is the point: one current rises exactly as much as the other falls.
steps.why: With the input voltage and the series resistance fixed, the total current is fixed. The zener therefore takes whatever current the load does not, which keeps the drop across the series resistance the same and holds the output steady.
common_mistakes: Saying the zener current also falls. It rises by exactly the amount the load current falls.
Saying the output voltage falls with a bigger load resistance. It stays constant — that is the regulation.

recall.must_convey: That when the load current changes the zener current changes by an equal and opposite amount, holding the output constant.
accept: zener current change is minus the load current change
the zener takes up the difference
load current falls so zener current rises
reject: all of the extra current goes through the zener

steps.memory_tip: The zener takes whatever the load leaves — the sum never changes.

steps.label: Input voltage changes
lines: The load current is fixed, so from (1):
If the input voltage increases, the supply
current increases, and all of that
increase passes through the zener. The
extra voltage is dropped across the
series resistance, so the output voltage
stays constant.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. All the extra current goes to the zener; the extra voltage goes to the series resistance.
steps.why: In breakdown the zener's voltage barely changes however much current it passes, so it can absorb the whole current increase without letting the output voltage move. The series resistance is what converts that extra current into the extra voltage drop.
common_mistakes: Saying the output voltage rises with the input voltage. It does not — that is the regulation.
Saying the extra current goes through the load. The load current is fixed here.

recall.must_convey: That when the input voltage rises the whole current increase goes through the zener and the extra voltage is dropped across the series resistance, so the output stays constant.
accept: the change in supply current equals the change in zener current
extra voltage appears across the series resistance
reject: zener current change is minus the load current change

steps.memory_tip: Case i: the zener trades current with the load. Case ii: the resistor eats the extra volts.

insider_note: The two cases are the marked part. Write both, and in each one name what stays constant and what absorbs the change.
